summary: Chunked request + oversized tracing headers cause API Gateway proxy buffering and idle timeouts leading to 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 504 gateway timeouts and increased tail latency for long-running chat completions. Issue appears correlated with clients sending chunked transfer requests and very large tracing/correlation headers (X-Trace-Baggage). Impact:
- ~12% of requests from NimbleDocs in us-west-2 are failing with 504 or returning after >30s delay.
- Affects production inference for redwood/gpt-7b-v2-quant used in assistant completion flows.
Environment:
- Prod, us-west-2, Hosted API (edge -> API Gateway -> NLB -> serving pool)
- API Gateway: AWS ALB in front of Nginx proxy instances (managed by infra team)
- Customer client uses chunked transfer with streaming and attaches large tracing baggage headers (~9–12 KB)
Observed behavior:
- Requests with headers >8KB frequently trigger proxy buffering in Nginx and cause the ALB to hit idle timeout waiting for backend bytes; ALB returns 504. Other cases show 502 when header truncation occurs upstream.
- When using small headers or non-chunked uploads, errors drop to baseline.
Expected behavior:
- Chunked streaming requests with reasonable tracing headers should proxy through with streaming responses and not hit the ALB idle timeout.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use client that sends a chunked POST to /v1/streams with streaming body and large X-Trace-Baggage header (~10KB).
2) Initiate a completion that takes >8s of backend processing before first bytes of response are flushed.
3) Observe ALB logs for target: response_code 504 and note ELB status code vs target status code.
4) Repeat removing trace header (or reducing to <2KB) and observe success and streaming behavior.
logs:
- ALB access log extract (2026-03-12T08:33:21Z): request_processing_time=0.002 target_processing_time=31.214 elb_status_code=504 target_status_code=504
- Nginx error log: "[error] 12345#0: *987 client aborted request, client: x.x.x.x, server: api, request: \"POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\""
- Nginx proxy_buffering debug: wrote 8192 bytes to proxy temporary file
- Serving runtime trace: request received, processing started, first token sent at +28s (but connection already reset)
- Packet capture (attached) shows client -> ALB sends headers then small body chunks; ALB establishes backend connection but does not forward until certain conditions due to buffering config.
investigation:
Hypotheses:
- Large request headers exceed proxy_buffer_size and proxy_buffers in Nginx, forcing buffering to disk; combined with chunked transfer and backend delayed flush causes ALB to perceive idle connection and close.
- ALB idle timeout (configured at 60s) interacts poorly with Nginx buffering behavior; if Nginx doesn't forward first backend bytes promptly ALB times out.
Findings:
- Reproduced in staging by sending 10KB X-Trace-Baggage header with artificial 25s delay before first backend write -> ALB returned 504 consistently.
- Reducing header to 1.5KB or tuning Nginx proxy_buffer_size to 16k eliminated buffering and restored streaming.
- No evidence of serving-runtime CPU slowness; the delay was artificial in tests, but production shows similar timing during heavy KV-cache warmups.
Next steps:
- Short-term workaround: ask customer to trim tracing baggage below 4KB and enable periodic early flush (send an initial chunk) to avoid ALB idle.
- Mid-term: infra to evaluate increasing proxy_buffer_size and adding ALB connection_draining/longer idle timeout for streaming routes; consider disable proxy_buffering for /v1/streams.
- Add defensive metric: count requests that trigger proxy temporary file writes and correlate with 5xx rate.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:17 - Support (Ava Chen): Opened with customer logs attached. Mentioned they saw spike in 504s starting 2026-03-10 after SDK update that added extra trace baggage.

2026-03-12 10:03 - SRE (Marcus Patel): I reproduced in staging with large headers + delayed backend flush. Nginx proxy_buffering sent to disk after 8KB which delayed backend handshake to ALB. Suggest temporary patch: disable proxy_buffering on stream endpoint.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Customer (NimbleDocs, Elena Rossi): We can trim the header size, but SDK change is org-wide and not easy to revert. Requesting a server-side fix.

2026-03-13 08:22 - Infra (Priya Kumar): Ran a config experiment on canary Nginx to increase proxy_buffer_size to 16k for streaming route. Preliminary tests show reduced proxy temp file writes and no 504s in replicated scenario.

2026-03-14 07:55 - Support (Ava Chen): Notified customer of workaround (trim trace header to <4KB) and that infra is testing canary config. Customer accepted workaround temporarily. Keeping ticket open while canary runs.
resolution: Workaround provided: customer to trim tracing headers and add initial chunk flush. Infra to deploy canary change to increase proxy_buffer_size for streaming routes and disable proxy_buffering for /v1/streams if stable. Follow-up: infra to present post-canar y results and proposed permanent config change. Ticket will be closed after canary is validated in prod for 48 hours.
